title: Automated measurement of lamellar thickness in human bone using polarized light microscopy
author: Ryan, Shefelbine, et al.

steps.title: Collect bone specimens
steps.instruction: Obtain bone specimens from individuals aged 5–26 years undergoing orthopedic deformity correction surgery; collect control bone from 5 patients without molecular abnormalities and osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) bone from 8 patients, using intact lower‑extremity long bones removed during osteotomy and intramedullary rod insertion.

steps.title: Prepare bone with glycol methacrylate
steps.instruction: Fix specimens in 10 % neutral‑buffered formalin for 3 weeks, decalcify in 25 % formic acid until soft, cut segments ≤15 mm × 7 mm × 7 mm along longitudinal or transverse cortical axes, infiltrate in glycol methacrylate (JB‑4 medium, JB‑4 embedding kit, Polysciences) for several weeks, embed in JB‑4 plastic, section at 5 µm thickness using a Microm HM 350 rotary microtome (Microm International GmbH), and stain sections with 1 % toluidine blue.

steps.title: Prepare bone with paraffin (optional)
steps.instruction: Fix and decalcify as above, then cut cortical bone along longitudinal or transverse axes, pass through increasing concentrations of alcohol, infiltrate and embed in paraffin, cut sections at 7 µm thickness, and stain with either 1 % toluidine blue or hematoxylin and eosin.

steps.title: Capture polarized‑light images
steps.instruction: Image the stained bone sections under polarized light at 20× magnification and save the raw image files for further processing.

steps.title: Draw initial rectangle in cellSens
steps.instruction: Open each acquired image in cellSens Entry, use the ‘perpendicular lines’ tool to draw two sides of a rectangle around the measurement area—one line parallel to the lamellae and the other perpendicular—applying the RGB color code specified for these lines.

steps.title: Complete rectangle and burn‑in
steps.instruction: Copy the two perpendicular lines, paste them without rotation to form the missing sides of the rectangle, use the ‘burn in info’ tool to make all four sides permanent, then save the annotated image as a .tif file and close cellSens.

steps.title: Add colored corner pixels in Paint
steps.instruction: Open the .tif file in Microsoft Paint, select the pencil tool at 1‑pixel size, recolor the two top‑corner pixels of the yellow rectangle with RGB (237, 28, 361.6) (red points), and recolor the two opposite corner pixels with RGB (34, 177, ?) (green points) as indicated; then save the edited .tif file.

steps.title: Run automated lamella measurement
steps.instruction: Open the MATLAB automated measurement script, set the variable ‘filepath’ to the edited .tif file location, run the script to generate Fig. 4, visually determine the expected numbers of bright and dark lamellae by inspecting the top row and counting bands horizontally until a band is cut off by the bottom frame, assign those counts to ‘xnBrightLamellae’ and ‘xnDarkLamellae’, run the script again, and record AvgBrightLengths_um, AvgDarkLengths_um, nSets, and ngSets; note that MATLAB will display six processing figures, with the sixth showing the final measurement image and excluded columns.
